title: Simulate credential expiry, renewal and revocation
prompt: Implement solve(payload) for a deterministic local credential lifecycle. ttl_s must be positive. events contains {"time_s":number,"kind":"issue"|"refresh"|"revoke"|"check","token":string}. Events are processed in input order. issue creates/replaces the token with expiry=time_s+ttl_s, clears revocation, and outputs "issued". refresh succeeds only for an existing unrevoked token with time_s<expiry, replacing expiry with time_s+ttl_s and outputting "refreshed"; otherwise output "denied". revoke outputs "unknown" if absent; otherwise marks it revoked and outputs "revoked", even if expired or already revoked. check outputs "unknown" if absent, else "revoked" if revoked, else "expired" if time_s>=expiry, else "active". Return {"outcomes":[one output string per event]}. Equal timestamps preserve input order; issuing again is an explicit new credential generation using the same synthetic identifier. Validate all input before processing, in this order: nonpositive ttl_s -> {"error":"invalid_policy"}; any unknown kind -> {"error":"invalid_kind"}; any negative/decreasing timestamp -> {"error":"time_order"}. Tokens are synthetic identifiers, not live secrets. Any numeric inputs are finite; inputs have the documented shapes; unspecified validation is out of scope. Do not mutate payload or any nested value. Numeric absolute tolerance 0, relative tolerance 0; strings, booleans, errors and collection shapes must match exactly.
